title: Landing hooks — engineering velocity & predictable inference economics
summary: Working draft: landing page hero and supporting copy that leans into engineering velocity and predictable inference economics. Goal is to craft hooks that resonate with infra/platform/ML engineers who evaluate vendors on latency SLOs, cost per token, and operational controls. Not final — rapid A/B candidates and rationales included.
primary_message_goal: Convey that Redwood lets engineering teams ship LLM features faster while keeping operational cost and reliability predictable — same API across hosted, dedicated, private.
hero_variants: Ship LLM features faster, keep costs predictable — one runtime for hosted, dedicated, and private
Build for users, not for inference ops — predictable latency and unit economics out of the box
Turn models into product features: production SLOs, cost controls, and rollout tooling for engineering teams
supporting_bullets: Consistent API across hosted, reserved, and private deployments — swap infrastructure without rewriting code
Latency SLOs and automatic fallbacks keep features live under load
Smart batching and KV caching reduce token cost without changing prompts
Per-route cost and latency breakdowns to debug regressions and optimize spend
audience_segments: Platform engineers — care about predictable throughput and integration with infra
ML engineers — care about model quality, KV cache behavior, and efficient serving
Product engineers — care about time-to-ship and consistent behavior across regions
competitive_notes: Position against three buckets: 1) hyperscaler managed endpoints (good infra but lock-in + coarse cost controls), 2) simple LLM API providers (fast to try but limited enterprise controls and private options), 3) self-hosted inference stacks (full control but high ops cost). Key differentiation: production-grade serving runtime + unified deployment modes + engineer-first observability. Avoid calling out vendors by name; use feature contrasts: 'no vendor lock-in, predictable unit economics, rollout controls'.
objections_and_responses: Objection: 'Why not host ourselves?' — Response: Hosting buys control but delays shipping; Redwood reduces ops work with optimized runtime and migration abstractions so teams focus on product features.
Objection: 'We need on-prem for compliance' — Response: Private deployment option with customer-managed VPC and KMS integrations; same API and tooling as hosted so rollout is seamless.
Objection: 'How do I trust cost claims?' — Response: Provide transparent unit-cost dashboards, token-level breakdowns, and reproducible benchmark kits for customer workloads.
test_hypotheses: H1: 'Engineering velocity' hero will increase sign-ups that proceed to API key creation by 15% vs generic 'cost and latency' hero
H2: Including a short metric line (e.g., 'typically 2–5x throughput on common LLMs') improves trial-to-conversion for platform teams
H3: Adding a CTA variant 'Run your workload in 5 minutes' will lift click-through for developer docs by 20%
sample_meta_description: Redwood Inference — production-ready LLM serving for engineers. Predictable latency, transparent unit costs, and one API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
CTA_variants: Try the hosted API — free credits
Deploy to your VPC — schedule a private demo
microcopy_snippets: Latency SLOs that you can set and monitor
Pin a model version, run a canary, rollback automatically
Per-token cost breakdowns to find spend hotspots
Seamless switch from hosted to dedicated without code changes
layout_notes: Hero should be concise with a single metric or benefit line, then three horizontal feature cards (Latency & Reliability / Cost Controls & Optimize / Deploy Anywhere). Secondary CTA row for enterprise vs self-serve. Add a small trust row with logos and a sentence about SLAs.
content_gaps_and_next_steps: Need: benchmark language for common use cases (chat, embeddings, reranking) with numbers; design comps for hero variants; copy testing plan with GA events. Next: sync with Applied ML for throughput claims (Evan), get design mockups (Sofia), create tracking ticket (GTM-402).
notes_to_self: Keep language engineer-forward (metrics, SLOs, rollout controls). Avoid marketing hyperbole like 'the best', focus on measurable outcomes. Save longer product detail for below-the-fold expandable sections.
footnote: Draft — internal only. If we include throughput numbers, must be verified by Applied ML and SRE before publishing.
